solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rotter giving frank description of curate's food?

definitions.meaning: a rotter is a scoundrel, a thoroughly nasty person
the curate's egg was 'good in parts', a polite way of saying it was off; said frankly, it was spoiled

explanation.surface: A cad's blunt verdict on what a clergyman was served for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The curate's egg comes from a Punch cartoon in which a nervous curate, served a stale egg by his bishop, says it is 'good in parts'. Said honestly, it was simply off.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a scoundrel is called a bad egg, a person gone rotten.

clue.text: Bishop has to make hasty departure: results in rebuff

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rush off is to leave in a hurry

explanation.surface: A bishop leaves in a hurry, and the upshot is a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rebuff is a curt rejection or dismissal.

clue.text: As teacher performed start of play, with minimum of creativity

parts.note: did as in 'did a turn', performed
Act I is the opening section of a play

indicators.note: the least of the word creativity is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone acted the opening of a play in a dull, schoolmasterly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: behaving in an instructive, lecturing manner, the way a schoolmaster would.

clue.text: Bunch of criminals shut up, any number imprisoned

indicators.note: the number is locked up inside the word for silencing

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Criminals silenced and locked away in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group of crooks working together is a mob or band.

clue.text: Party politician in protest against Conservative scoundrel

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a protest march
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A party politician marches against a Tory villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the US party opposed to the Republicans is a party politician.

clue.text: Troublesome former English sailor, poisonous type in hiding

parts.note: ex means one-time, previous
an asp is a venomous snake
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: An ex-navy man causes trouble with a venomous snake concealed about him.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a British naval term for an ordinary sailor, not an officer; 'in hiding' tucks the snake in after the English letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something troublesome is irritating or maddening.

clue.text: Honest and lacking any slant

definitions.meaning: literally flat and horizontal, with no tilt

explanation.surface: Honest and unbiased, an even-handed account.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something genuine and above board is said to be straight; literally, a surface that is perfectly flat.

clue.text: Minister about to go to court with men

parts.note: re means concerning, about
OR (other ranks) are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A clergyman is about to go to court accompanied by some men.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a minister of religion in charge of a parish is a parish priest of this title.

clue.text: Delightful experience with country finally getting agreement

parts.note: a treat is something especially enjoyable

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word country is taken

explanation.surface: A pleasant outcome as a nation at last signs a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal pact between states.

clue.text: International organisation dead with unity ruined

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
unity is the number one

explanation.surface: The United Nations is finished, its unity in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who is undone is ruined or destroyed.

clue.text: Soft thing that is minute

definitions.note: a phrase describing something very tiny, standing in for a noun

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for soft
an article is an item or thing

explanation.surface: A soft object that happens to be extremely small.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'thing': read together, 'thing that is minute' describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a speck or tiny piece of matter is extremely small.

clue.text: Country's leader restricted by changes and noisy arguments

indicators.note: the letter is confined within the word for changes

parts.note: alterations are modifications, changes

indicators.note: the leader of the word Country is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nation's head is constrained by reforms, and there are rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: heated quarrels or disputes.

clue.text: Kick person suffering from overwork

definitions.meaning: in rugby, to ... is to kick an opponent's shins
a drudge, a writer or worker hired to do dull, heavy work

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a kick at the shins, and a drudge who churns out work.

clue.text: Drank nothing, dashed outside, being exhausted

indicators.note: the word for dashed wraps around the drinking and the zero

parts.note: dashed as in raced off, cut away
a cat lapped its milk, drank
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone drank nothing and rushed out, worn to a frazzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: worn out, knackered, broken down.

clue.text: Son forming an alliance, becoming less transparent?

parts.note: teaming up is joining forces

explanation.surface: A son joins forces with others and grows harder to see through.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: windows or glasses fogging over become less transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: glass misting with condensation is losing its clarity.

clue.text: The friend at a dance lacking courage

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend at a dance who is too timid to ask anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a dance' reads like a location, but 'at a' are letters to rearrange and only 'dance' signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: timid, cowardly, without nerve.

clue.text: Male in agony embraced by female supplying drug

indicators.note: all of that is held within the female animal

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit

indicators.note: the male letter is placed inside the word for agony

parts.note: agony is intense pain

explanation.surface: A man in pain is cradled by a woman giving him medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: a neurotransmitter also given as a medicine, so a drug.

clue.text: Perhaps the Derby apartment has a group of people

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
a race is a people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Derby-town apartment houses a community.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race at Epsom, run on the flat, without jumps; the 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Derby is a horse race run without jumps.

clue.text: Deal with problem, being exceptionally noble and ethical

indicators.note: taken as 'in an exceptional way', so these letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: Tackling a difficulty by being outstandingly upright and moral.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to deal decisively with a festering problem, as a doctor drains an abscess.

clue.text: Rare church gets damage on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the damage word sits above the church

parts.note: to scar is to mark or damage
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rare church that has suffered damage to its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scarce means in short supply, seldom found.

clue.text: As a group once reassembling outside old car firm

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the car firm
the letters of once are put back together differently

parts.note: BL was British Leyland, the former UK car maker

explanation.surface: A group once again put together around an old car manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' reads as 'formerly' but is the anagram fodder; British Leyland was a former UK car maker, which 'outside' places within.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French phrase meaning all together, collectively.

clue.text: Little girl that's happy to go round in uniform

indicators.note: the word for happy encircles the little girl

parts.note: content means satisfied, happy
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A small girl content to wander around in her school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing, but here it is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: steady, unvarying, the same throughout.

clue.text: Mass in provisional from Dean initially rejected

indicators.note: that letter is thrown out of the word for provisional

parts.note: a draft is a provisional version

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Dean is meant

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean turns down a provisional order of Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass sounds like a church service, but it means a large quantity, as in 'a raft of measures'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large number or amount of something.

clue.text: Beetle landing on a lady

indicators.note: in a down entry the beetle sits on top of the letter

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle

explanation.surface: A beetle alights on a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's first name, so a lady.

clue.text: District in which priest supplants eastern system of belief

indicators.note: the priest takes the place of the eastern letter

parts.note: a region is an area or district
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A district where a clergyman replaces an Eastern faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a faith, an organised set of beliefs about the divine.

clue.text: Famous rider keen to return after travel

indicators.note: the eager word follows the travelling one

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: the word for keen comes back the other way

parts.note: avid means keen, eager

explanation.surface: An eager horseman sets out on a journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry in protest at her husband's taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the noblewoman remembered for a naked ride on horseback.

clue.text: Spies act suspiciously, being in denial of reality

indicators.note: acting suspiciously, so these letters behave out of order

explanation.surface: Secret agents behave shiftily, refusing to face facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: seeking fantasy to avoid unpleasant truth.

clue.text: Cell barrier penetrated by this person

indicators.note: the setter's self pierces the barrier

parts.note: a gate is a barrier
the setter refers to himself, so this person is me

explanation.surface: A prison cell's barrier broken through by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison, but it is a biological reproductive cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: a sperm or egg is a reproductive cell.
